title: The Interview Remembered
description:
Your second interview at a different company.

One of the interviewers leaned forward.
'You said something in a previous interview that caught our attention — can you elaborate?'

Something you'd said in a prior application had made it into a reference. You'd told the truth that day.

choices.text: Explain consistently — the same answer as before
choices.result_text:
It matched. The interviewer nodded.

Telling the truth doesn't mean the answer has to be polished. It means the answer is the same every time it gets checked.
The only story you never have to remember is the one you didn't make up.

choices.text: Try to soften it — the truth might come off wrong now
choices.result_text:
The interviewer frowned slightly.

That divergence — even a small one — was enough to raise a question.
It was a small thing. But trust is often built or broken in small things.

title: The Interview Caught Up
description:
At the team dinner, a coworker mentioned something casual.

'Your résumé said you did X — that's interesting.'

{name} went still.
That wasn't something they'd done. It was something they'd said in an interview.

choices.result_text:
Harder than expected. But it actually went better than expected.

There's a version of the lie that stays buried forever. This wasn't that version.
Owning it sooner hurt less than being found out later.

choices.text: Deflect — find a way to change the subject
choices.result_text:
Got past it. This time.

But that conversation left a small crack. Trust that gets quietly repaired is still cracked.
The lie is still there. Now someone else is close enough to notice.

title: The Day the Pattern Broke
description:
The savings account hit a number {name} had only thought of as hypothetical.

Standing at the bank terminal, staring at the figure.

This started from choosing not to spend ₩7,000 on delivery. Repeatedly.

choices.result_text:
The money stayed where it was.

Saving isn't just numbers. It's proof that you can commit to something without immediate reward.
That discipline will transfer to every decision from here.

Spent some of it. Felt good.

There's a version of saving that becomes self-punishment. That's not sustainable either.
Just don't let 'reward' become the habit that was given up.

title: The Chart That Mattered
description:
The first real position. Not practice, not theory.

Watched the price move.

{name} felt something that wasn't in any book about investing.
The gap between knowing and doing.

choices.text: Let it run — trust the analysis
choices.result_text:
Didn't touch it. Checked it less.

The hardest part isn't buying or selling. It's the waiting in between.
Investing patience turned out to be a skill too.

choices.text: Take the small profit now — better than watching it reverse
choices.result_text:
Sold early. It went higher afterward.

Classic. But the lesson isn't 'hold forever.' It's 'know your reason.'
The real mistake was not having a plan before buying.

title: Running on the Wrong Fuel
description:
Running on envy had worked. Until it didn't.

Today at the investment screen, {name} caught themselves not seeing opportunity — just seeing what other people had.

Envy had been the engine. But at some point, all it burned was the driver.

choices.text: Acknowledge the shift — find a different reason
choices.result_text:
'I started this because I wanted to prove something. That's not enough anymore.'

Reasons that come from fear run out. Reasons that come from vision don't.
This was harder to articulate. But it lasted longer.

choices.text: Push through — the results don't care about the motivation
choices.result_text:
True. The market doesn't care why you make a good trade.

But the body does. And the mind does. And the people around you eventually notice.
The results kept coming. The cost kept accumulating.
